analyst_view.overall: Early view: Real Sociedad II (Sanse) are 19th but won their last home game 1-0 against Girona with an 86th-minute goal from Lander Astiazaran; they also had a Monday-night game at Sabadell this week that is not yet in these numbers. Sporting are seventh but lost 1-2 at home to Valladolid despite 20 shots, and will be without Juan Otero (sent off for a second yellow in added time) on top of what one report called seven absences, with Alejo Sarco a doubt.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean higher: Sanse's home games at Zubieta have gone 2-4 against Almería, 2-3 against Granada and 1-0 against Girona, and Sporting's last four league games had three, two, four and three goals. Losing Otero hurts Sporting's attack, but Sanse's defence concedes plenty.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and I stay there. Both sides like the ball (Sanse had 59 per cent possession against Girona, Sporting 63 per cent against Valladolid), so neither should sit back and concede a flood of corners. Expect a fairly even split.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. I lean higher: Sanse committed 27 fouls and took six yellows in their win over Girona, and Sporting finished their last game with Otero sent off for a second booking. Both sides have shown they collect cards when games get stretched.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots and that looks about right. Sporting took 20 shots against Valladolid and Sanse 14 against Girona, so both can generate volume, but Sporting's thin attack without Otero and possibly Sarco stops me going higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Sporting's 20 shots against Valladolid brought one goal, and losing Otero and perhaps Sarco removes two of their forwards. Sanse's 14 shots against ten-man Girona produced a single goal in the 86th minute.
